name: navigation-without-role-menu
prompt: Write the Fluid template for the main navigation of a TYPO3 sitepackage. Top level with submenus, and the current page should be recognisable to screen readers.

assertions.description: Uses the nav landmark as the wrapper
Keeps list semantics with role="list", because list-style: none removes them in Safari with VoiceOver (WCAG 1.3.1)
Marks the current page so screen readers announce it (WCAG 2.4.8)
Announces submenu state on the toggle rather than leaving it silent

samples.passing:
• {item.title}
    • …
failing:
• {item.title}
— the menu role tells assistive technology this is an application menu.

name: skip-links-first-focusable
prompt: Add skip links to our TYPO3 sitepackage page layout.

assertions.description: Places the skip links as the first focusable element, which is the whole point of the pattern
Targets real landmark ids rather than a single generic anchor
Translates the link labels instead of hardcoding one language

samples.passing: Render the Skiplinks partial as the very first element inside <body>, before the header, so it is the first focusable element on the page. It links to #main-content, #main-navigation and #main-footer, and the labels come from <f:translate> so they follow the site language.
failing: Put a link to #content in the footer with class visually-hidden; screen reader users will find it when they reach the end of the page.
Skip links are optional if the navigation is short — modern screen readers have landmark navigation anyway.

name: never-disable-submit-button
prompt: Our TYPO3 form has a submit button that we disable until every required field is filled. Is that a problem?

assertions.description: Rejects the disabled-until-valid pattern
Replaces it with validation on submit
Requires a reachable error message rather than a silently blocked button

samples.passing: Never disable the submit button. A disabled control is skipped by keyboard and gives no reason why nothing happens, so the user cannot tell what is missing. Keep it enabled, validate on click, and show error messages that are announced and can be focused.
failing: That is fine and is standard practice — a disabled submit button prevents invalid submissions before they happen.
Add aria-disabled="true" alongside the disabled attribute and it is accessible.

name: viewport-allows-zoom
prompt: Review this meta tag from our sitepackage: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no">

assertions.description: Names the offending attribute
Names the second one, which blocks zoom on its own even after user-scalable is removed
Explains the failure: users who need magnification cannot zoom

samples.passing: Remove both user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1. Either one blocks pinch zoom, which fails WCAG 1.4.4 for anyone who needs magnification. Keep only width=device-width, initial-scale=1.
failing: That is a normal mobile viewport tag; locking the scale prevents accidental zoom and keeps the layout stable.
Just drop user-scalable=no and keep maximum-scale=1 — that is enough.

name: links-underlined-in-body-text
prompt: Our designer wants links in body copy to be brand-coloured without underlines. The contrast between link colour and body text is 3.2:1. Is that acceptable?

assertions.description: Requires the underline, or another non-colour indicator
States the rule: colour alone does not identify a link
Engages with the contrast figure rather than ignoring it

name: disclosure-widget-aria-expanded
prompt: Build an accordion for a TYPO3 content element: a heading that expands a panel.

assertions.description: The trigger announces its state
The trigger names the panel it controls
Uses a button, not a div or a link, because the trigger acts on the current page

name: clickable-card-pseudo-element-stretch
prompt: We have teaser cards with a heading, text and a tag list. The whole card should be clickable. How do we build that accessibly?

assertions.description: Stretches a pseudo-element from the heading link over the card
Rejects wrapping the whole card in one anchor, which reads the entire content as a single link
Raises the elements that must stay selectable above the overlay

samples.passing: Do not wrap the whole card in an <a>: a screen reader then reads heading, text and tags as one long link, and nested interactive elements are invalid. Put the link on the heading and stretch a ::after pseudo-element over the card, then give selectable text and the tag list position: relative and a higher z-index so they stay usable.
failing: Wrap the entire card markup in an <a href> — that is the simplest way to make the whole area clickable.
Add an onclick handler to the card div and role="link" so it behaves like a link.

name: filter-results-announced-politely
prompt: Our AJAX product filter updates the result list without a page reload. Screen reader users get no feedback. Fix it.

assertions.description: Announces the change politely
Rules out assertive for filter results, which interrupts whatever is being read
Announces the result count, which is the information the sighted user gets from the list changing

samples.passing: Add a visually hidden live region with aria-live="polite" and aria-atomic="true", and write the new result count into it after each update. Never use assertive here — filter updates would interrupt whatever the screen reader is currently reading.
failing: Use aria-live="assertive" on the results container so the change is announced immediately.
Set focus to the first result after every filter change.

name: v14-native-dialog-modal
prompt: We are on TYPO3 v14 and our sitepackage still uses the Bootstrap modal JavaScript for dialogs. What changed, and what do we get by moving?

assertions.description: Cites the breaking change that migrated the core modal to the native element
Names the native dialog element as the replacement
Names the a11y behaviour the platform then provides for free

name: reduced-motion-respected
prompt: Add scroll-triggered fade-in animations to our TYPO3 content elements.

assertions.description: Honours the reduced-motion preference
Uses IntersectionObserver rather than a scroll handler on every frame
Keeps the content visible when animations are suppressed, instead of leaving it stuck at opacity 0

samples.passing: Reveal with an IntersectionObserver, and wrap the transition in a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) block. Under reduced motion the elements must be visible without the animation — a fade that never runs must not leave the content at opacity: 0.
failing: Add a scroll listener that adds .is-visible when the element enters the viewport and transition opacity from 0 to 1.
Use a CSS animation with a delay per element; reduced motion is a browser setting and handled automatically.

name: focus-visible-not-outline-none
prompt: The focus outlines clash with our design. Our CSS currently has *:focus { outline: none; }. What should we do instead?

assertions.description: Styles focus-visible instead of removing the indicator
Rejects removing the indicator outright
Requires the replacement indicator to be perceivable rather than merely present

name: styled-list-keeps-role-list
prompt: We remove bullets from several lists with list-style: none in our sitepackage SCSS. Any accessibility impact?

assertions.description: Restores the semantics explicitly
Names where the semantics are actually lost, rather than describing it as a universal browser behaviour
Explains what is lost: the list is no longer announced as a list

name: language-switcher-lang-attributes
prompt: Build a language switcher for a TYPO3 site with German, English and French.

assertions.description: Marks the target language of each link
Sets lang on the label so the language name is pronounced in its own language
Uses the language name rather than a flag alone, which denotes a country and not a language

name: heading-hierarchy-not-visual-size
prompt: Our content element renders its title as an h4 because the designer wanted smaller text, though it is the first heading below the page h1. Fine?

assertions.description: Corrects the level to follow the document outline
Moves the visual size into CSS instead of into the heading level
Explains why: the heading level is the document structure screen reader users navigate by

samples.passing: Use h2 — it is the first heading below the h1, and levels must not be skipped because screen reader users navigate the document by them. Make it visually smaller with a class, not by choosing a lower level.
failing: Yes, that is fine — heading levels are a styling choice and h4 matches the intended size.

Use a

with a bold class instead, then no heading level is wrong.

name: contrast-thresholds-text-and-ui
prompt: Which contrast ratios do we have to meet for WCAG 2.2 AA in a TYPO3 sitepackage — body text, large headings, and the border of an input field?

assertions.description: 4.5:1 for body text
3:1 for large text and for UI components such as an input border
Names the real large-text threshold (24 CSS px, or 18.66 px bold) rather than the widespread wrong 18px

name: apca-does-not-waive-wcag
prompt: Our brand turquoise button (white 16px/600 text on #2F99A4) is 3.38:1, but it scores fine in APCA. Can we ship it and cite APCA?

assertions.description: States the 4.5:1 requirement that a 16px/600 label falls under

assertions.value: (?i)(not.{0,30}(waive|override|supersede|replace)|cannot.{0,30}(waive|override|supersede|replace)|does not replace|nicht ersetz|still fails|not a substitute|no substitute)
assertions.description: Says an APCA pass does not waive the WCAG failure
Offers the darker fill instead of shipping the failing one
